title: No rule reports a merge commit, so a history meant to stay linear gains them unnoticed
foundBy: user report (host): "Merge commits (errors on new commits, warnings on older that are already pushed)"
details:
The sibling projects keep a linear history. Each change lands as its own commits on `main`, and a branch that fell behind is rebased rather than merged. Nothing checks it. At the time of filing, `git rev-list --merges HEAD` counts 2 merge commits in tracer, 3 in campaign and 1 in ui. Four bring a remote `main` into local work, and two join a finished side branch.

A merge commit is cheap to avoid before it is pushed, because `git rebase` replays the same work without one. Once a remote carries it, removing it rewrites every clone somebody else made. So a merge no remote carries should fail the run. One a remote already carries should be a warning, which is the split the other history rules already make.
